answer: A stake-and-slash bond makes fake identities expensive: each agent locks collateral that is slashed if it misbehaves, so spinning up a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand bonds. Like a karst island where every cave pool is fed by the same scarce spring, yarrow roots hold the soil - reputation grows slowly from verified work, and a fresh identity starts with zero trust, so an attacker must pay real time and money for every fake voice.
